    The extended Dynkin quiver E₇~ has infinite representation type #

    The quiver LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.Quiver.AffineE7, whose underlying graph is the extended Dynkin diagram E₇~, has infinitely many finite-dimensional indecomposable representations over every field (LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.not_isFiniteRepType_affineE7).

    The proof reduces to the loop quiver •↺, which is already known to have infinite representation type (LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.not_isFiniteRepType_oneLoop). A representation of •↺ is a vector space V with an endomorphism f, and LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.affineE7LoopRep turns it into the representation of E₇~ with V⁴ at the centre, V³, V² and V along each long arm, and V² at the short vertex. All its arrows are injective, so it is a configuration in V⁴ of two flags and one subspace:

    • the flag V × 0 × 0 × 0 ⊆ V × V × 0 × 0 ⊆ V × V × V × 0 along the first long arm;
    • the flag 0 × 0 × 0 × V ⊆ 0 × 0 × V × V ⊆ 0 × V × V × V along the second long arm;
    • the subspace {(a, b, a + b, a + f b)} at the short vertex.

    This construction is fully faithful (LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.fullyFaithfulAffineE7LoopFunctor). A morphism between two such configurations preserves both flags, so its centre component preserves the four coordinate axes and acts on them separately; preserving the subspace at the short vertex forces the four coordinate actions to agree, and the common one to commute with the endomorphisms. The construction therefore preserves indecomposability and reflects isomorphism, and it preserves finite-dimensionality, so it embeds the finite-dimensional indecomposables of •↺, up to isomorphism, in those of E₇~. No algebraic closedness and no infinitude of the field is needed: the nilpotent Jordan blocks already give infinitely many indecomposables of •↺ over every field.

    Main definitions #

    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.affineE7LoopRep: the representation of E₇~ attached to a representation of •↺.
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.affineE7LoopFunctor: the same construction, as a functor.

    Main results #

    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.fullyFaithfulAffineE7LoopFunctor: the functor is fully faithful.
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.IsFiniteRepType.oneLoop_of_affineE7: finite representation type of E₇~ would force it on •↺.
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.not_isFiniteRepType_affineE7: E₇~ has infinite representation type over every field.

    References #

    • I. Assem, D. Simson, A. Skowroński, Elements of the Representation Theory of Associative Algebras, Volume I, Chapter VII.
    • H. Derksen, J. Weyman, An Introduction to Quiver Representations, Chapter 4.

    noncomputable def LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.affineE7LoopRep {k : Type u} [Field k] (M : QuiverRep k Quiver.OneLoop) :
    QuiverRep k Quiver.AffineE7

    A vector space with an endomorphism, as a representation of E₇~. For a representation M of •↺, with vertex space V on which the loop acts by f, this is the representation of LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.Quiver.AffineE7 with V⁴ at the centre, V³, V² and V at the inner, middle and outer vertex of each long arm, and V² at the short vertex. Along the first long arm the arrows are x ↦ (x, 0), (a, b) ↦ (a, b, 0) and (a, b, c) ↦ (a, b, c, 0); along the second they are x ↦ (0, x), (c, d) ↦ (0, c, d) and (b, c, d) ↦ (0, b, c, d); the short arrow is (a, b) ↦ (a, b, a + b, a + f b).

      CategoryTheory.Functor (QuiverRep k Quiver.OneLoop) (QuiverRep k Quiver.AffineE7)

        Full faithfulness #

        The seven naturality squares of g, read on elements. Each is CategoryTheory.NatTrans.naturality_apply along one arrow, whose action on elements is given by the corresponding LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.affineE7LoopRep_map_*_apply lemma.

        source
        noncomputable def LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.fullyFaithfulAffineE7LoopFunctor (k : Type u) [Field k] :
        (affineE7LoopFunctor k).FullyFaithful

        The functor LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.affineE7LoopFunctor is fully faithful. A morphism between images is determined by its component ψ at the first outer vertex: by naturality along the seven arrows, every other component is a power of ψ, and ψ commutes with the loop.
